question: Why is there no insistence on grasping or rejecting sense objects for one established in supreme Bhairava consciousness?
premises: Purity and impurity are not intrinsic realities but relative designations.
For one whose nature is supreme Bhairava consciousness, sense objects do not bind by their own status.
Enjoyership surges forth spontaneously from that consciousness itself.
inference: Because enjoyership arises spontaneously from supreme Bhairava consciousness, there is no insistence on either grasping or rejecting sense objects.
plain_english: Therefore there is no insistence at all on either grasping or rejecting sense objects; for one whose nature is the consciousness of supreme Bhairava, enjoyership surges forth by itself.
